channel.title: Posts on Sven Eisenschmidt - Personal Blog
channel.description: Recent content in Posts on Sven Eisenschmidt - Personal Blog

item.title: Heat
item.description: Poor Aika is suffering with the heat. The hot ground will turn her feet to little stumps of coal, and the usually cold floor in the kitchen is climbing up to 30°C too.

item.title: Downstairs
item.description: The rooms under the roof have been hitting 35°C, so we moved the boys downstairs into the cold playroom that stays shut all day. It is funny how a different sleeping spot sparks this much joy and excitement in them. At 35°C upstairs, I might just sneak down and join them.

item.title: Climate
item.description: Temperature and oxygen management of the house has become our side gig. Not sure if I should be happy that the inside temperature only gets up to 28°C throughout the day.

item.title: Stop Gap Sparrow
item.description: Recovered my streak with a Sparrow I met in the wee hours.

item.title: Munich
item.description: Two-day office visit at the roadsurfer HQ in Munich.

item.title: Fort
item.description: We love a good pillow fort.

item.title: Sandbox
item.description: All the work around the sand pit and removing the old pond paid off. It hits 35°C during the day at the moment, so water is allowed in the sandpit too.

item.title: Good Night, Swallow
item.description: Swallows, swallows everywhere. Impossible to photograph when flying, easy when they are sitting. I caught these at sunset.

item.title: Mixed Bag
item.description: This post is a bit of a mixed bag: more kestrel content, Hypo 1.11, a Sigma USB dock, and barn owls.

item.title: Excursion
item.description: The local NABU chapter called me late in the afternoon, out of the blue, asking if I wanted to join a trip in their “Treffpunkt Naturschutzdienst” format, this time to the grazing project at the “Aufschlussgraben”, Werben. It is a closed-off area meant to restore local wildlife and serve as a compensation area for the heavily farmed fields around it. The big tease was the breeding ground of 50 bee-eater couples, a bird I aspire to photograph.

item.title: Hypo 1.10
item.description: Hypo 1.10 is out, with better support for Nikon cameras and it’s various MakerNote implementations, Fujifilm RAF files, and autofocus points on Canon bodies.

item.title: Sponsor Post: Nadine's Morning at the Pond
item.description: Nadine visited the “magical” grey wagtail pond yesterday and was greeted with a variety of birds: red kite, grey wagtail, red-backed shrike, common redstart. She walked from one end to the other, chasing a golden oriole and a cuckoo, but neither sat for a photo.

item.title: Hypo is Live
item.description: Hypo got its first public release and goes live with a website. Grab Hypo for free there.

item.title: Sit-in
item.description: Today I did my first sit-in at a pond. Nadine had reliably seen a grey wagtail on her commute over several days, so while Tilian was at sports, I used the time to settle down by a quiet stretch of water, with dead trees and slightly flowing water.

item.title: Warming Up
item.description: Spent last night fine-tuning the settings of the Canon R5 and I see myself getting more out of it compared to yesterday. The Sigma telelens combined with the RF-EF dapter seems to have issues with AF. I learned there are likely two issues, first AF pulsing and second a desync between the body image stabilization and the built-in lens one. Before trying out further I’ll update the firmware of the Sigma telelens, yes lenses have firmwares these days - what a time to be alive, and disable the body image stabilizer.

item.title: First Steps
item.description: I did the first steps with the R5: firmware upgrade, settings, sooo many settings. Overall this is a new setup to learn and it will take a while to master. Especially the Sigma seems to behave slightly differently with the EF-RF ring.

item.title: Gemma
item.description: Anthropic pulled Fable and Mythos from the market following US intervention, a frustrating move considering Fable was performing for me like Opus was six months ago, before the steady performance degradation across versions 4.6+. It really makes me wonder where LLM proliferation needs to go to ensure we aren’t tied to these frontier labs.

item.title: R5
item.description: I finally settled on an R5 I. After a lot of fun with the 1D-X II, I had been thinking for a while about how to get around the limitation of its 20MP sensor, and shooting the Sigma at f/8, where it is sharpest, I kept hitting the limit of how much detail I can pull out of a single frame.

item.title: Archive
item.description: I am consistently one day behind in posting a daily photo. This is from a second tour I made to see the kestrels in the barn across the street, this time with the Sigma TC-1401 1.4x teleconverter on the camera. My original plan was to find Nadine’s old BlackBerry Bold. I wanted to charge it and try it out after watching that BlackBerry movie which surprisingly wasn’t too bad. Liked it more than The Social Network. Taking daily photos that inspire me and feel genuine became a chore, I am forcing myself to keep doing them.

item.title: Resting
item.description: Kellin is home sick with a fever, spending his days resting on the couch. He is the most cute and grumpy when sick, and it’s sad when you can only do very little to make him feel better.

item.title: Sandbox
item.description: At 8pm 3.5 tonnes of sand finally arrived for the sandbox, and by 10:45pm 3 tonnes of it had disappeared into the hole. Finally we can see the end of the project. From here it’s fine work: filling the edges, irrigation, a lid for the cistern, lawn edging and plants, lots of plants.

item.title: Bumblebee
item.description: We found an exhausted bumblebee in our house, and Nadine used the Beevive kit I had brought back from my trip to Jasper in April to revive the little one. For the next hour the bee did not want to leave her side.

item.title: Mushrooms
item.description: Nadine grew her first mushrooms, and they were good.

item.title: Kestrels
item.description: We spent the whole day in the garden on the old pond area, the sand pit is now officially fenced in with robinia logs and all the uneven ground around it is filled up with topsoil, and on Monday I order the next 1.5 tonnes of sand for the sandpit itself.

item.title: Soapbox Race
item.description: Tilian had his yearly soapbox race, and over the past weeks he and Nadine built a rather good little cart together, light, with wheels that roll well and quick to steer, but they had no chance to field test it, and on the day it turned out the cart did not handle gravel well, which is what the loop around the kindergarten is made of. Bummer. With everything they learned this year it should be enough for a podium spot next year.

item.title: Race to (No)where(?)
item.description: Jasper sent me a post on AI enthusiasts and skeptics, the enthusiasts racing against time and the skeptics racing against entropy, and Jasper and I turned it into a funny metaphor about electric cars.

item.title: Hike
item.description: I went on a 15 km hike, I had the day off as it is a public holiday in Bavaria and I follow that schedule rather than the local Saxonian one. Half way through the hike Nadine picked up Aika, she deserved a break and I hadn’t had a single good shot on the Canon anyway - So I had to continue.

item.title: Stork
item.description: Saw mother stork watching over her chicks on my morning tour with Aika, someone local, can’t remember who, shared the fledglings already leave the nest for a few minutes at a time. That would make a great shot.

item.title: Rose
item.description: The battery of the Rose Reveal would not charge anymore, the same dead brick on wheels I wrote about earlier, so I finally brought it to a Rose service partner in Leipzig. I had not expected the verdict to be “there is nothing we can do here, here are your pedals and attachments”, the bike gets sent in and then we will see.

item.title: Water
item.description: I felt dizzy all day, so Nadine kept reminding me, loudly, to drink more water, and Tilian joined in by parroting her, slipping me secret notes that read “Mer Wasser!!!” (more water).

item.title: Markfest
item.description: We went with Nadine’s parents to the Kulinarisches Marktfest in Groitzsch, where the Kellin made it straight for the bouncy castle, had no interest at all in the clown show, and Tilian set off on his own little tour.

item.title: Starling
item.description: Tilian had another Nature Detectives day at the NABU, learning about herbs and finishing around the campfire with Stockbrot (bread baked on a stick). I used the time to photograph the local starling family while the everyone were busy. It took a lot of patience (which I am not very good at), but I caught the mother flying in to feed her young every minute or so. She lingered only a moment each time before setting off again.

item.title: Blackcap
item.description: An early start at work and a late finish. Before work I took a long walk above the meadows, hoping to find the red-backed shrike again. He kept out of sight, but a blackcap sat still long enough for me to photograph it instead.

item.title: Fledgling
item.description: It is a good day when I manage a sharp picture of a bird, even better when Jasper and I send each other sharp wildlife photos on the same day.

item.title: Shrike
item.description: The battery of the Rose e-roadbike is dead, it has turned into a heavy brick on wheels. Why did I opt for an e-bike again? We’ll never know.

item.title: Poppy
item.description: After weeks of searching I finally found the male pheasant. Whenever I am out on a morning tour I can hear him without ever managing to locate him, and today I found out where he likes to roam, though he vanished into the tall grass just as quickly as I caught a glimpse of him. Next time I’ll get you. So a poppy for today instead.

item.title: Lazy
item.description: We had a lazy day. Nadine went for a photo walk but it did not yield any good photos. It gets more and more difficult to spot birds with the dense foliage. The boys and I visited my parents down the village, and we spent the rest of the day watching movies.

item.title: Knights Games Trebsen
item.description: Went to see the annual Knights Games in Trebsen. We left Aika at Nadine’s grandmother and drove to Trebsen, west of Leipzig. We had been there four years ago over Pentecost but didn’t make it to the actual joust back then.

item.title: Nuthatch
item.description: The nuthatch was as surprised as I was. Neither of us was prepared to be so close to each other. A quick burst shot later with the Canon, and we went our own ways.

item.title: Breakfast
item.description: Two guys enjoying their breakfast. It was a usual Friday. More pond work ahead this long Pentecost weekend, and fingers crossed for a successful photo walk in the forest to break the series of mediocre pictures. I can hear a woodpecker from the kitchen window.

item.title: Overcast
item.description: The weather is beautifully erratic, it just swings between sun, wind and rain all day.

item.title: Sparrows
item.description: Sparrows are both fidgy (difficult to photograph for me) but also plenty here, so it’s an easy target for a daily photo if you are patient. It was raining most of the day yesterday so sparrows sought shelter in our garden in the large pine tree and under the swing. I wonder if they realize how goofy they look.

item.title: Bounce
item.description: Took a lucky shot today of a fox jumping 500m away from me through the tall grass. Too far away, too blurry, too dark; yet I am delighted that I caught the moment by accident.

item.title: Cliché
item.description: Nadine and I were joking today, as we are approaching our 40s, that we start spending money on typical things: cameras, road bikes, coffee machines, birding stuff, sourdough and furniture in millennial grey. So here we go, we got a new coffee machine and I have been fiddling around with it for two hours already to realise the espresso beans we have are actually not espresso beans. I promised Nadine she will have her light-as-water coffee also with this machine. The clock is ticking against me on this one.

item.title: Scouting
item.description: Trying out different paths in the morning to scout new places to take pictures of the local birds. Aika is getting more careful each tour and starts to sneak alongside me.

item.title: Cistern
item.description: Nadine and I have been crushing it on the pond excavation site. After yesterday’s placement of the cistern we finished plumbing and started sculpting the space. We moved a ton of sand today.

item.title: Big Friday
item.description: After a busy week I had Friday off. I went out early to get pictures of the local foxes and a pheasant I have been hearing every now and then. Couldn’t find either. Rest of the day we continued removing our old pond. We got the new 500L cistern in place, which is a big step forward. Plumbing next.

item.title: Tradition
item.description: Back home after a reliable five hour drive. Picked up as the tradition requires a book for Tilian and toy car for Kellin. Received a self-made father’s day from Tilian in return. Soundtrack of the drive: Vanna - A New Hope.

item.title: Offsite
item.description: Spent twelve hours in a meeting room. The countryside venue helped.

item.title: Hotel
item.description: Back in Bavaria close to Munich for a two-day strategy offsite. When I joined trivago in 2016, and ever since at Appsfactory, Delivery Hero and now roadsurfer, I have been routinely traveling inside and outside of Germany.

item.title: Nadine's Birthday
item.description: It’s Nadine’s birthday. We talked about it last week. We spoke about it on the weekend. This morning the boys and I forgot about it and left the house without saying anything. What a terrible family. We don’t deserve her.

item.title: Guided Bird Song Hike & 840mm
item.description: Last week left me feeling that even a good camera kit doesn’t guarantee inspiration or good photos. I was looking forward to today’s trip to break the loop of dissatisfying pictures.

item.title: The Jury Experience
item.description: Nadine and I got to spend the day in Leipzig all by ourselves.

item.title: Fox & Wagtail
item.description: Contemplating to get an used Sigma TC 1401, could bring details I just don’t have during post-editing cropping.

item.title: Puddle
item.description: Nadine went out with the boys.

item.title: Greenfinch
item.description: Nadine got a shot of a greenfinch.

item.title: Forest Stroll
item.description: Went with the boys and the dog to the forest.

item.title: Sparrows
item.description: Sparrows. Sparrows Everywhere.

item.title: Canon Selphy
item.description: Got the Canon SELPHY CP1500 to print our favourite daily photos for the photo wall at home. I printed the first batch of postcard-sized prints from last week’s trips today.

item.title: Saros
item.description: After a long day in the garden, arguing with the PayPal chatbot about why my claim from when I was scammed has been denied (but I am not giving up yet), I was ready to get back to Saros’s first boss and beat it. It’s a great game and a more accessible version of Returnal, except for the difficulty level.

item.title: Stork
item.description: One of the two local storks looking for small rodents and amphibians shortly after the meadow had been freshly mowed.

item.title: Blackbird
item.description: Got today’s daily photo. A blackbird sitting on our garage, 2 meters away from my office window. Easy and convenient.

item.title: Long Day
item.description: Long day at work in Munich and going back tomorrow at dawn to Leipzig.

item.title: Big Day
item.description: Twenty-four hours later, I am back on a work trip in Munich for two days. Took the Canon 1D X Mark II for the first tour in our local forest: a fox cub, a group of deer, a Eurasian jay, a starling, a barn swallow and a long-tailed tit.

item.title: England, Day 4 1/2
item.description: Back home after a great time with Jasper and his family. Will be coming back during the summer holidays with our campervan. With the risk of repeating myself, flying has become a very smooth experience, 20 minutes from touchdown to the train at BER.

item.title: England, Day 4
item.description: We strolled through the Brighton Car Boot Sale. In many ways things are similar in Germany and the UK. Car boot sales are one of them. Saw an N64 (they guy wanted £50!) and a Sega Mega Drive.

item.title: England, Day 3
item.description: Jasper and I wanted to see the windfarm close to Brighton since a while. We went there today.

item.title: England, Day 2
item.description: The day nicely separated into three activities and peak busyness: we went to the RSPB Pulborough Brooks to take pictures, visited Dan (Hi Dan!), Jasper’s business partner, and went to the movies to see Project Hail Mary (second time).

item.title: England, Day 1
item.description: Arrived safely in Brighton, Jasper and I went out straight for a photo tour through the hills above Rottingdean.

item.title: Departure
item.description: Going to visit Jasper & family for a long weekend, back on Monday. Not sure when we started this tradition but keeping it alive by taking turns every year became a big part of our friendship. The flipside: getting up at 4am tomorrow.

item.title: Rolling
item.description: Went with Tilian and Aika on a stroll through the fields and the local forest. Encountered a Heron, a Magpie and a pair of Starlings. I would love to get a good shot of a Magpie, one day!

item.title: Split
item.description: Three days to my trip to the UK. The week is nicely split between wrapping up work and packing for it. Surprisingly it is also the busiest work week. I guess you can’t plan for that.

item.title: Rooster
item.description: Rainy day in the garden and our mechanical rooster doesn’t mind. It spins like a windmill in any breeze, so I shot at 1/2000s to freeze it (1/250 would have worked too). It’s been raining all Sunday and it’s my first daily photo in the rain. Next Sunday I hit 100 daily photos.

item.title: Nature Detectives
item.description: Once a month Tilian is joining a program called Nature Detectives. It is organized by the local NABU chapter.

item.title: Alpha
item.description: Switched from the Sony RX100 VII to a Sony Alpha 6400.

item.title: Station Visit
item.description: On the feet from 4am to 10pm. The founders of roadsurfer and us non-founding executives spent the day at the Nürnberg station.

item.title: Redstart
item.description: Saw a young black redstart this morning on our roof.

item.title: Blossom
item.description: Spring is in full swing and I am ready for it. I got my new travel passport and ETA for the UK. 1 1/2 weeks to go.

item.title: Back to Back
item.description: All day back to back in meetings - high season is coming and we are setting goals for the last push before summer peak. Rushed out between breakfast and first calls on the go with Aika and capture a heard of sheeps chilling in the rain.

item.title: Jump
item.description: Tilian testing gravity. Almost forgot about today’s daily photo, that’s a first.

item.title: Mufflon
item.description: A Mufflon. Nadine’s nick name for me was mufflon when we got together. This year it will be 15 years since then.

item.title: Artemis
item.description: Jasper send me earlier a nice video about the Artemis II photos: ‘Explaining the Most Important Artemis II Photos’, conincidentially I got for Tilian, ok for myself, one of the LEGO Artemis sets. Nadine and I went out on a short photo walk, today’s photo is sponsored by her with post editing by myself.

item.title: Scammed
item.description: Last week I did not pay attention and entered my personal data with pictures of my travel passport into a fake UK government website to request my ETA for my forthcoming trip. Call me an official idiot.

item.title: Milestone
item.description: I have been using the Sony more over the last days. The Canon’s softness and zoom distort my perception of how good the Sony actually is, especially the finer and sensitive grain adds a nice character to the Sony. Switching between both is fun.

item.title: Star
item.description: Back to running a birder website. I got lucky this morning with a Stork and a Starling

item.title: Flyby
item.description: A red kite passed a few meters above us on our Easter walk today. It was stormy, so the large birds stayed low.

item.title: Duck
item.description: I spotted this friendly duck in a small pond today.

item.title: Experimental
item.description: I ran the photo import in an experimental Hypo branch today and I will learn from my mistakes: the photos never arrived in Apple Photos and got deleted from the card. Update: I was able to recover them.

item.title: Loop
item.description: Working on Hypo and immediately using new features in my photo workflow is instant gratification, and it becomes a self-reinforcing loop.

item.title: Two Cameras
item.description: I went out this morning with both cameras, the two bird shots from the Canon and the frost on the bridge from the Sony.

item.title: Dissolve
item.description: One of the new windmills north of the village, dissolving in the mist. If you’re looking for something to read, Jasper published a good reflection about AI and his craft, and sent his March recap newsletter. And I successfully avoided any April fools jokes today.

item.title: Low
item.description: The last few evenings went into building Hypo and the Dragon Touch setup. Agentic coding is a different kind of effort: the cycles from idea to working product are so fast that you barely notice how much you are putting in.

item.title: Dragon Touch (Pt.2)
item.description: A follow-up to the Dragon Touch post from a few days ago, about two things that bothered me enough to fix.

item.title: So I Built a Mac App
item.description: Nadine and I shoot a lot of photos. A lot in the sense that we are still beginners and have quite an amount to sort through every time. But the amount of pictures is not what this is about.

item.title: Village Walk
item.description: A walk through the village with friends. Spring was showing up everywhere, the light has been so good again.

item.title: Packed
item.description: Today was packed, in the morning I went out to use the fantastic weather to get some good shots of birds again, the usual Sparrow and a first time shot of a Goldfinch.

item.title: Dragon Touch
item.description: We got a Dragon Touch 27" digital display to use as a family calendar. My original plan was to build something with an e-ink display and a Raspberry Pi Zero, but this felt like the faster path.

item.title: Grace
item.description: Jasper sent me the STL file for a Ryland Grace figure from Project Hail Mary. Project Hail Mary is, for me, the best film I have seen in years, and I can barely wait for the home cinema premiere.

item.title: Kite
item.description: I’ve been avoiding working from my office space for the last three weeks. I overdid it on the walking pad a few weeks ago, and both kitchen and winter garden were more enjoyable with the warmth of the sun.

item.title: Green
item.description: I picked this one at random from today’s shots and liked it for the framing and the minimal colors, and for the fact that there are no birds in it for once.

item.title: Principles
item.description: One of my team leads came to me today with a proposal. I gave feedback, we talked it through, and at some point we laughed about whether it would be possible to know in advance what my reaction would be, whether my thinking was consistent enough that you could predict where the pushback would land before talking to me.

item.title: Blue Sky
item.description: A starling on the roof, a sparrow on a cable, and a red kite overhead, all three on the same blue day. Nadine caught a great shot of the red kite. I think we are both pushing what we can get out of the 90D and the 250mm lens.

item.title: Dodge
item.description: My father restores vintage cars as a hobby, and today we did a photo shoot together. The car is a 1932 Dodge Eight Series DK, fully restored by him.

item.title: Fog
item.description: A quick morning tour with Aika trough dense fog before a full day of building furniture. Writing this just before 9pm, still not done, lights next and then putting everything back in.

item.title: Dusk
item.description: A great tit on the evening walk with Aika. Low light, but it still worked out.

item.title: Blackthorn
item.description: A photo of a blackthorn, just coming into bloom. I am finding more and more enjoyment in dialing in settings manually, aperture, shutter speed, ISO, and seeing what comes out.

item.title: Sponsored Post
item.description: Today was back to back, morning to evening. Today’s photo is sponsored by Nadine from her photo tour. If you look closely you see two sparrows.

item.title: Pigeon
item.description: Spent most of today’s energy on a new blog post. But the light outside was too good to ignore, so I grabbed the camera and tested different manual settings for aperture, shutter speed and ISO. Not a fan of pigeons, but I am happy with the sharpness on this one.

item.title: Change as a Commodity
item.description: I’ve been trying to answer a question about AI and software development for a while now, and I don’t think I’ve been looking far enough for an answer.

item.title: Building This Website with Hugo (Pt. 2)
item.description: A few months of running this site in production and things changed. This documents what and why, and hopefully saves someone who is just starting out with Hugo some time. The first post covers the initial setup: Building This Website with Hugo.

item.title: Monday
item.description: This is what a successfull Monday looks like: Booked my flights for April to see Jasper and his family. Decided to go for a Sigma 600mm lens. Fell asleep 8pm with the kids during bedtime routine.

item.title: Requiem
item.description: I finished Resident Evil Requiem on the PS5 Pro. It’s a 8/10 for me.

item.title: Mühltal
item.description: Nadine was away for the last weekend of her Wildnispädagogik training. The boys and I spent the morning at the Mühltal.

item.title: Privilege
item.description: Every Friday afternoon, Nadine’s parents pick up Tilian and Kellin. There is no fixed plan. Sometimes it is an outing, sometimes an hour of card games.

item.title: Tilian's Favourite Spot
item.description: Tilian got the task from school to choose his favourite place where he lives. Nadine went to take a picture of it with him. To my surprise, it’s the same spot I spent a lot of days as a kid.

item.title: Aika
item.description: We had parents’ evening at school. I asked to go on the school’s roof to take a picture of the historic water tower. It was dark, all images were blurry. So here is picture of Aika isntead. Nadine said there will be the time for a good shot of the water tower. It was not today.

item.title: Stork
item.description: I am trying really hard not to let this website become a bird-blog. But the storks are back!

item.title: Night Shot
item.description: Inspired by Jasper’s night shots and a video I saw on youtube last week that had a nice segment on post-processing night shots I tried to see what I can get out of the Sony RX100 VII.

item.title: Honeybee
item.description: Heard a swarm of insects humming and was surprised to find a bunch of honey bees on a willow catkin that early this year.

item.title: Buntspecht
item.description: Got a shot of a great spotted woodpecker. Almost gave up getting a good shot of anything today.

item.title: Overflight
item.description: A plane passing overhead I saw today while taking the dog out for a long afternoon walk. Much like me, flying into the weekend after an eventful week. The vignette effect in the picture was not intentional and I like how it came out naturally.

item.title: Rime
item.description: I walked the dog this morning, same as every day. The world feels caught between winter and spring right now. There’s still frost overnight, double digits by afternoon. How am I supposed to decide what jacket to wear?

item.title: Perpetual
item.description: Went for a walk in the woods with the neighbors and their dachshund, and Aika. Spotted a pheasant, a fox, a red kite, and a few deer.

item.title: No One Was Driving The Car Tour
item.description: Went to see La Dispute playing their No One Was Driving The Car Tour in Leipzig today. They played King Park and Adria which made me happy.

item.title: Coloss
item.description: Did a late-afteroon trip with Tilian to the big bucket-wheel excavator. He was mesmerized by the size, unfortunately it stopped operating for the day.

item.title: Song Thrush
item.description: It’s not my intention to turn this website into an animal-focused photo blog, but here we go. Spotted a song thrush this morning. First thought it was a female blackbird.

item.title: Wild Horses
item.description: We drove to see wild horses. It’s a nature reserve one hour south-west of Leipzig. It’s called the Toten Täler (Death Valleys).

item.title: Upgrade
item.description: Upgraded from an iPad Air 13" and a Mac mini (M2) as my usage centered more and more around photo editing and agentic coding. The Mac mini feels too static and the iPad too limiting.

item.title: Moon
item.description: Nadine and I shot the half moon tonight. Otherwise an ordinary day, looking forward to a packed Friday and weekend. I asked her for a text for the post, she said: This is the moon. Sometimes you see it when it’s dark, sometimes even when it’s bright. Sometimes you see it never at all. (very SMRT)

item.title: Deer
item.description: Managed to capture a young deer in the nature reserve yesterday.

item.title: Lost Americana Tour
item.description: Nadine and I went to Berlin to see MGK’s Lost Americana tour. I did not bring a proper camera. In hindsight I could have.

item.title: Emma
item.description: Emma lives in the next village and goes absolutely berserk behind her gate whenever we walk by. She could slip underneath it any time she wanted, but the moment the gate actually opens, she’s the shyest dog you’ve ever seen.

item.title: Zootopia 2
item.description: Tilian and I went to see Zootopia 2 today. We are big fans of the Die drei ??? Kids audiobooks and wanted to watch the movie of the main series, but the trailer had some scary scenes that Tilian doesn’t like so we opted in for a more relaxed movie. Once the new Die drei ??? hits streaming we will give it a try at home.

item.title: Woods
item.description: I went back to the woods looking for the white albino deer, and found a white albino doe instead.

item.title: Weir
item.description: Nadine and I went out on a photo walk today. We spotted a few animals but couldn’t get any good shots. We ended up at Weiße Elster weir (51.124943, 12.236676).

item.title: Dawn
item.description: I took Aika for a long walk at dawn this morning, carrying Nadine’s Canon with our new Canon EF-S 55-250mm F4-5.6 IS STM tele lens.

item.title: Afterburner
item.description: A few days ago, out of nowhere, I remembered a game I played at my cousins a lot, it was After Burner II on their Sega Mega Drive. I have been looking to scratch that itch on a Steam Deck.

item.title: Stump
item.description: Old tree stump next to the agriulture road out of town.

item.title: New Games
item.description: Last week brought a bunch of new games and demos. Pragmata was my favorite and will be a day one purchase for me.

item.title: Spare Parts
item.description: The front bumper of Tilian’s RC car broke off today. Kellin broke it, but to keep the peace I told Tilian it was me.

item.title: Back Home
item.description: We made it back from Mayrhofen. Around 550 km, about six and a half hours with one break and a short traffic jam along the way, which is pretty reasonable for that distance.

item.title: Winter Vacation (Pt. 7)
item.description: Last full day in Mayrhofen. A round of Hus, a Mario Kart World cup, three groups heading in different directions and Tilian finally spending his pocket money.

item.title: Winter Vacation (Pt. 6)
item.description: Mountain day for everyone. We rode up the Penken together, Tilian took second place in his ski school race, Aika had her five minutes of fame and we closed out the evening at Goldkind.

item.title: Mayrhofen at Night
item.description: Nadine and I had an evening out in Mayrhofen. On the walk home, we stopped for a few neon sign photos.

item.title: Winter Vacation (Pt. 5)
item.description: Kellin was back on his feet. We spent the morning walking along the Ziller, rode the Zillertalbahn home and ended the evening at an escape room.

item.title: Winter Vacation (Pt. 4)
item.description: Kellin woke up with a fever, so my father-in-law and I stayed back with him while the others hit the slopes.

item.title: Winter Vacation (Pt. 3)
item.description: Up at 5. Getting better.

item.title: Optimizing Hugo Builds
item.description: I keep original camera JPEGs in my Git repo. A Sony RX100 VII and a Canon EOS 2000D, files between 4 and 8 MB each, sitting right next to the markdown. Hugo resizes all of them on every build. 273 images at last count. On GitHub Actions that meant over two minutes per deploy, most of it spent on image processing that produced the exact same output every time.

item.title: Winter Vacation (Pt. 2)
item.description: Day two started at 4:30 in the morning. The older one couldn’t sleep anymore. Great start to a vacation day.

item.title: Winter Vacation (Pt. 1)
item.description: We made it to Mayrhofen. Around 600 km, about 7 hours on the road with two short breaks. The drive was smooth, nothing to complain about.

item.title: School's Out
item.description: Tilian got his mid-year report card for second grade. Straight A’s in all main subjects and conduct marks.

item.title: Black Ice
item.description: Lots of black ice on the farmers road and large chunks of frozen snow on the sides which looked like icebergs. It’s been below zero for weeks and quite enjoyable. I dread when it all melts and gets wet again.

item.title: Bubblegum Blue
item.description: Saw this bubblegum-blue tractor during my daily tour with Aika. Everything is brown and dark in winter and I am a sucker for some color during my walks.

item.title: Wolf Tracking
item.description: Nadine went wolf tracking last weekend and took great shots. It took place across the Czech border and was organized by two wildlife academies: Funkenflug and Heidefeuer.

item.title: Abandoned
item.description: Came across this abandoned place. The window color (tm) gives it a nice contrast.

item.title: Overtaken
item.description: I went for a two-hour walk with Aika, didn’t get any good shots except the usual brick-buildings from across the river (51.140149, 12.230809). After two hours, a group of older road cyclists passed me, dropped a cheeky comment and sped off.

item.title: Melt
item.description: Nadine went to Czechia to learn about tracking of wolves and other animals. She took the Sony RX100 VII and I got to use her new Canon EOS 2000D. The kids kept me busy inside and outside, the only shot that I eventually kept was the one of snow slowly melting down our greenhouse.

item.title: Pheasant
item.description: Went for a long walk and did some meetings from the phone while the light was great outside. Saw a pheasant, a young buck and heron.

item.title: Two Dorks
item.description: Two dorks outside in our garden. Photo courtesy of Nadine.

item.title: Blue
item.description: I have been trying to be more active in the last days, averaging around 16.000 steps each day, both treadmill supported but also more walks with Aika. Today I came across this blue net hanging ourside of a barn and I just could not figure out what it’s supposed to do.

item.title: Kohlmeise
item.description: I thought this is a decent picture of a Kohlmeise (google the english name yourself - not going to use it here) but then remembered Jasper’s pictures of birds (1, 2) he took and felt ashamed.

item.title: Soft
item.description: Fresh snow fell overnight, so naturally, you get a snow photo the next day. It has always been this way, and it always will be.

item.title: Imagination
item.description: Love this kid. Kellin can take a half-broken toy, a pile of week-old snow and immerse himself in a new adventure so easily.

item.title: Cake
item.description: We needed to cancel Tilian’s kids birthday party on short notice due to last-minute guest-to-be cancellations of 66% of participants. Fortunately the cake was already prepared and needed to be taken care of appropriately.

item.title: Mine (Pt.2)
item.description: I went back to the open-cast mining ground and found a great spot to photograph these massive steel giants that have scarred the landscape.

item.title: Windpark (Pt.2)
item.description: Hello Windpark my old friend! Next to walking in the mornings outside with the dog, I get to walk even more indoors now. We got a treadmill at home since yesterday and I spent my meeting-packed day walking.

item.title: Ambiguity
item.description: Ambiguity gets a bad reputation at work, and people treat it like something is broken. “There’s no clear direction.” “Leadership doesn’t have a plan.” I’ve sat in meetings where someone said exactly that, and I’ve read the same feedback in employee surveys for years. (And I take it somewhat personally as I am that “leadership”.)

item.title: Tilian’s 8th Birthday
item.description: Tilian turned 8! Time flies so fast. We spent the afternoon building a decommissioned LEGO (42097) set I have been hunting online for him for a while. The bags are not numbered!

item.title: Bricks
item.description: Week started well at work and I can use the morning hours again for a longer walk with Aika before hitting the desk. Winter mornings don’t offer great light, yet it’s the only time I have to take pictures during week days.

item.title: Mine
item.description: Tilian and me went to take pictures of the ‘open-cast mining ground’ close to our village.

item.title: So I built an RSS Reader (Pt.2)
item.description: Two weeks ago I wrote about building an RSS reader. I said it would probably crash with more than 20 feeds (or I lose motivation). It didn’t crash but I needed to optimize it a bit.

item.title: Frost
item.description: Last night’s frost laid a soft film over all surfaces.

item.title: New Camera Day
item.description: The Sony RX100 VII is here! I took it out for a spin with the kids to the forest and the garage of my father. There is so much to learn about it.

item.title: Disappointed
item.description: The Sony RX100 VII did not arrive today. I rescheduled delivery from yesterday to today because of my work trip this week. Not sure what happened for it not to arrive but I’m disappointed.

item.title: Back
item.description: Completed my trip back home today. Did twice 450km within 24 hours. The VW California is such a comfortable car for long trips.

item.title: Away
item.description: Tilian is sick and Kellin has been quarantined as a precaution. I am on a work trip to Munich so it was extra difficult to leave them until tomorrow night.

item.title: Windpark
item.description: We have a new windpark north of our village. 250m high wind mills. The moon illusion hits hard with them, they overshadow the village from one end, and look tiny from the closer end. Strange to see.

Got two Speed Champion BTTF sets (#77256) for the boys. We watched the first two movies over the holidays for the first time with them and they loved it. Coincidentally Lego released this set January 1st.

item.title: Last Day Off
item.description: Vacation is over and I’m officially back at work tomorrow. A few impressions from today.

item.title: Craspedia globosa
item.description: Taken in our garden. […]Craspedia is a genus of flowering plants in the family Asteraceae commonly known as billy buttons, billy balls, and woollyheads. They are native to Australia and New Zealand where they grow in a variety of habitats from sea level to the Southern Alps.[…] (Wikipedia) - I’d would have called them yellow balls.

item.title: Vet
item.description: Neither Aika nor I woke up this morning and thought “Hey let’s rip out a toe nail, that sounds like fun!”. Yet here we are and we spent this afternoon at the vet.

item.title: Snow
item.description: First proper snow this season. The boys loved it. Aika was slightly annoyed.

item.title: So I built an RSS Reader
item.description: So I built an RSS reader. I wanted something simple for myself. Read my feeds, mark things as read, move on.

item.title: Reading
item.description: I don’t read enough books. I manage reading a few pages maybe one evening every two weeks. I can turn on something on Youtube or a podcast in the car without thinking. A book I have to actively pick up.

item.title: Sourdough
item.description: My wife started baking bread. Here’s her spelt (Deutsch: Dinkel) sourdough recipe. It took quite a few iterations to get it right.

item.title: Chicken
item.description: When I went out with Aika, I caught two of our four chickens in the garden. We have two Silkie chickens and two feather-footed dwarf chickens. The whole family loves them, and two eggs a day is a nice bonus.

item.title: Building This Website with Hugo
item.description: This website runs on Hugo, a static site generator written in Go. I launched it in early January 2026, so if you’re reading this when it’s fresh, this is all just a few days old. This post documents how I built it.

item.title: Winter Walk
item.description: A winter walk with Tilian and Aika. The fresh snow melted during the day but froze overnight, leaving icy patches everywhere. Plenty of slipping and sliding along the way, with the kids landing on their backsides more than once. Aika seemed completely unfazed.

item.title: 2025 Wrapped
item.description: My year 2025 in numbers and highlights, wrapped-style. First attempt at summarizing an eventful year. More platforms offering wrapped/replay summaries obviously helped.

item.title: Death Stranding 2
item.description: Over the Xmas period I managed to finish Death Stranding 2. The game is a perfect mix between logistics, base building and shooter action for me.I like it more than the Metal Gear Solid games.

item.title: Open Source
item.description: At the end of 2025 I spent 100 hours on a single open source project. I did similar things over the past twenty years but always lost interest. This time was different. The software is actually used at my company. Spoiler: I will happily discontinue it.

item.title: Hello
item.description: Welcome to my website. I work as Chief Technology & Product Officer at roadsurfer, where we help people explore the world in campervans.
